ds: Lawyers, accountants, trust and company service providers, brokers and other professionals may knowingly or unknowingly structure transactions, set up entities or move funds to help designated persons avoid sanctions. Indicators focus on unusual service patterns, pass-through behaviour and the enabler's own risk profile.

src.t: FATF, Guidance on Beneficial Ownership of Legal Persons (2023)
OFAC and UK government advisories on sanctions evasion enablers (general reference)

rat: Lawyers, TCSPs and brokers structuring and moving funds for designated persons; informal netting and barter also seen.

ind.n: Service provider incorporates many entities for related clients with shared structures
ind.cx: Same provider sets up numerous similar entities for linked beneficial owners.
ind.ds: A single provider, broker, lawyer or agent sets up entities or handles transactions for many related clients with similar structures.
ind.cn: Adviser or agent acting for multiple linked clients

ind.n: Professional's client account used as pass-through
ind.cx: Funds enter and leave client accounts of an adviser with no related service.
ind.fp: Client accounts are used for legitimate settlements.
ind.ds: A professional's client account is used to move funds with no underlying legal or advisory work.
ind.cn: Professional client account used as pass-through

ind.n: Advisers instructed to use complex structures after a customer's designation risk emerges
ind.cx: Request for restructuring after adverse news or risk of designation.
ind.ds: Request for restructuring after adverse news or risk of designation.

ind.n: Facilitator relying on informal channels, cash or trade offsets for clients
ind.cx: Payments for clients via netting, barter or unrecorded transfers.
ind.fp: Informal systems are used in some communities.
ind.ds: Payments for clients via netting, barter or unrecorded transfers.

ind.n: Provider with disciplinary history or enforcement exposure
ind.cx: Adverse regulatory or enforcement actions concerning sanctions handling.
ind.ds: Customer or principal has previous convictions, enforcement or disciplinary action, or has been exited by another institution.
ind.cn: Prior regulatory, criminal or enforcement history

ind.n: Provider acts for many clients from the same higher-risk jurisdiction
Fee arrangements disproportionate to services or paid by third parties

ind.cx: Applications or licence reliance appear inconsistent or altered.
ind.ds: Applications or licence reliance appear inconsistent or altered.

ctl.n: Gatekeeper and company service provider due diligence
ctl.ds: Assesses licensing, CDD standards and client mix of formation agents, lawyers and similar professionals and monitors formation volumes and concentration. It targets professional enablers.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.

ctl.n: Suspicion escalation and reporting decision protocol
ctl.ds: Defines timelines, owners and criteria for escalating concerns and deciding whether to report, and for documents implying payments to proscribed groups. It ensures timely, accountable decisions.

Detects funds that return to their origin or loop between linked parties through reciprocal, matched, netted or round-trip flows using graph analysis and account comparison. It exposes artificial turnover and loan-back structures.
Detects remitter-like activity, pooled flows and informal channel use on accounts not authorised for money transfer. It finds unregistered MVTS operators and hawala-type settlement.

Records control issues with owners and deadlines, escalates overdue items and independently confirms that remediation has worked before closure. It ensures weaknesses are fixed rather than merely logged.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.

Benchmarks agent commissions, rebates and fees, requires justification and compliance sign-off for payments in high-risk markets, and tests invoices for evidence of real services. It limits disguised bribery.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

Checks identity and supporting documents for tampering, forgery, template reuse and internal inconsistency, and corroborates their data against authoritative or reliable independent sources. It exposes altered or counterfeit credentials that pass a visual check.

Verifies licences, registrations and supervisory status of customers, agents and counterparties against regulator registers before onboarding and periodically. It confirms legal authority to operate and detects unlicensed activity.
